name: Assam
tagline: Where the Brahmaputra River meets the rolling hills of the Eastern Himalayas

topAttractions.name: Kaziranga National Park
topAttractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and home to the one-horned rhinoceros, Kaziranga National Park is a must-visit for wildlife enthusiasts.

topAttractions.name: Majuli Island
topAttractions.description: The largest river island in the world, Majuli Island is a haven for nature lovers and those seeking a peaceful retreat.

topAttractions.name: Umananda Island
topAttractions.description: A sacred island in the Brahmaputra River, Umananda Island is home to the Umananda Temple, a 17th-century temple dedicated to Lord Shiva.

culturalFact: Assam is the birthplace of the unique Sattriya dance, a classical form introduced in the 15th century by the great Vaishnavite saint Srimanta Sankardev.

hiddenGem.name: Biswanath Chariali
hiddenGem.description: A scenic town surrounded by tea gardens and the Brahmaputra River, Biswanath Chariali is a hidden gem for those seeking a peaceful retreat.

passportTieIn: If you have stamps from Kaziranga National Park or the Brahmaputra River, you might be interested in visiting the nearby state of Meghalaya, which is home to the stunning Mawsynram Falls and the beautiful Mawlynnong Village.

name: Goa
tagline: Where the sun meets the sea

topAttractions.name: Fort Aguada
topAttractions.description: A 17th-century Portuguese fort that now serves as a popular tourist spot and a former prison

topAttractions.name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
topAttractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most famous churches in India, housing the remains of St. Francis Xavier

topAttractions.name: Palolem Beach
topAttractions.description: A picturesque beach known for its crystal-clear waters, white sand, and vibrant nightlife

culturalFact: Goa's unique cultural blend is showcased in its Azulejos—hand-painted tin-glazed ceramic tiles brought by the Portuguese—that still adorn many historic homes and churches.

hiddenGem.name: Divar Island
hiddenGem.description: A tranquil island steeped in history and natural beauty, accessible only by ferry and offering a glimpse into old-world Goan village life.

passportTieIn: If you have stamps from the Portuguese colonial era or a wishlist item for a colonial-era fort, they will appear here!

name: Gujarat

topAttractions.name: Somnath Temple
topAttractions.description: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas in Hinduism, this ancient temple is a sacred site for devotees and a must-visit for its stunning architecture and spiritual significance.

topAttractions.name: Dholavira
topAttractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, Dholavira is an ancient Indus Valley Civilization city that offers a glimpse into the region's rich history and cultural heritage.

topAttractions.name: Gir Forest National Park
topAttractions.description: Home to the majestic Asiatic lion, this national park is a wildlife enthusiast's paradise and a great place for trekking and birdwatching.

culturalFact: Gujarat is the birthplace of the intricate Patola silk sarees of Patan, which can take up to a year to weave and are dyed using a complex double ikat technique.

hiddenGem.name: Little Rann of Kutch
hiddenGem.description: A unique salt marsh that is home to the endangered Indian Wild Ass, offering breathtaking sunset views and stark, beautiful landscapes.

passportTieIn: If you have stamps or wishlist items for Gujarat, you might also be interested in visiting the nearby state of Maharashtra, which is home to the iconic Ajanta and Ellora Caves, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Karnataka
tagline: Where ancient history meets vibrant culture

topAttractions.name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
topAttractions.description: A 240-acre botanical garden featuring over 1,800 species of plants and trees, including the famous Lalbagh Glass House.

topAttractions.name: Mysore Palace
topAttractions.description: A majestic palace built in the Indo-Saracenic style, featuring stunning architecture and beautiful gardens.

topAttractions.name: Hampi
topAttractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and ancient capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, featuring stunning ruins and temples.

culturalFact: Karnataka was the seat of the mighty Vijayanagara Empire, whose capital Hampi was one of the largest and wealthiest cities in the world during the 14th to 16th centuries.

hiddenGem.name: Aihole
hiddenGem.description: A small village famous for its ancient temples and ruins, often referred to as the 'cradle of Indian architecture'.

passportTieIn: If you have stamps or wishlist items for Hampi, Mysore Palace, or Bandipur National Park, they will appear here!

name: Kerala

topAttractions.name: Backwaters of Alleppey
topAttractions.description: Experience the serene beauty of Kerala's backwaters by taking a houseboat ride through the tranquil canals and lagoons.

topAttractions.name: Munnar Tea Plantations
topAttractions.description: Visit the picturesque tea plantations of Munnar, surrounded by rolling hills and lush greenery, and enjoy a cup of freshly brewed tea.

topAttractions.name: Padmanabhaswamy Temple
topAttractions.description: Explore the ancient and mysterious Padmanabhaswamy Temple, and marvel at its intricate carvings and architecture.

culturalFact: Kerala is renowned for Kathakali, a highly stylized classical Indian dance-drama recognized by its vibrant makeup and elaborate costumes.

hiddenGem.name: Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary
hiddenGem.description: A peaceful and serene bird sanctuary located on the banks of Vembanad Lake, home to a wide variety of bird species and offering stunning views of the surrounding landscape.

passportTieIn: If you have stamps from the Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary or the Athirappilly Waterfalls, you might want to consider visiting the nearby Munnar Tea Plantations or the Backwaters of Alleppey for a similar experience!

name: Maharashtra
tagline: The land of vibrant culture and breathtaking landscapes

topAttractions.name: Gateway of India
topAttractions.description: A 20th-century monument that symbolizes India's independence and a popular tourist spot in Mumbai.

topAttractions.name: Ajanta and Ellora Caves
topAttractions.description: Ancient rock-cut Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain caves that are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

topAttractions.name: Mahabaleshwar
topAttractions.description: A hill station famous for its strawberries, scenic views, and trekking trails.

culturalFact: Maharashtra has a rich tradition of folk theatre and dance, most notably Lavani, which is known for its powerful rhythm and energetic movements.

hiddenGem.name: Kanheri Caves
hiddenGem.description: A lesser-known Buddhist cave complex near Mumbai, featuring ancient sculptures and carvings.

passportTieIn: If you have stamps or wishlist items for Maharashtra, they will appear here!

name: Rajasthan
tagline: The Land of Kings, Where Royalty Meets Adventure

topAttractions.name: Hawa Mahal
topAttractions.description: A stunning example of Rajput architecture, this palace of winds is famous for its intricate latticework and stunning views of the city.

topAttractions.name: Jaisalmer Fort
topAttractions.description: A majestic fort built in the 12th century, this UNESCO World Heritage Site is a testament to the engineering skills of the Rajput era.

topAttractions.name: Lake Pichola
topAttractions.description: A serene and picturesque lake surrounded by majestic hills and beautiful palaces, offering breathtaking views and tranquil boat rides.

culturalFact: Rajasthan's cultural heritage includes the intricate art of blue pottery, which uniquely uses a dough of quartz stone powder instead of clay.

hiddenGem.name: Bishnoi Village
hiddenGem.description: A small village in the Jodhpur district, known for its unique culture and stunning natural beauty, where visitors can experience the traditional way of life of the Bishnoi community.

passportTieIn: If you have stamps or wishlist items for the Taj Mahal, you might be interested in visiting the stunning City Palace in Jaipur, which has a similar blend of Mughal and Rajput architecture.

name: Tamil Nadu
tagline: Where ancient temples meet modern charm

topAttractions.name: Brihadeeswara Temple
topAttractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the largest temples in the world, built in the 11th century by the Chola dynasty.

topAttractions.name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
topAttractions.description: A vibrant and colorful temple dedicated to the goddess Parvati, known for its intricate carvings and stunning architecture.

topAttractions.name: Marina Beach
topAttractions.description: One of the longest urban beaches in the world, stretching over 13 kilometers and offering stunning views of the Bay of Bengal.

bestTimeToVisit: The best time to visit Tamil Nadu is from October to February
culturalFact: Tamil Nadu is home to the ancient Tamil script, which dates back to the 2nd century BCE and is one of the oldest surviving scripts in the world.

hiddenGem.name: Kumbakonam
hiddenGem.description: A charming town on the Coromandel Coast, known for its beautiful temples, scenic canals, and traditional Tamil culture.

passportTieIn: If you have stamps from the Brihadeeswara Temple or the Meenakshi Amman Temple, you might be interested in visiting the other UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India, such as the Taj Mahal in Agra or the Hampi ruins in Karnataka.

name: Uttar Pradesh
tagline: The Heart of India's Rich Heritage

topAttractions.name: Taj Mahal
topAttractions.description: A stunning white marble mausoleum built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

topAttractions.name: Varanasi Ghats
topAttractions.description: A series of ancient riverfront steps and temples along the Ganges River, a sacred site for Hindus.

topAttractions.name: Agra Fort
topAttractions.description: A 16th-century Mughal fort and palace complex that served as the imperial residence of the Mughal emperors.

bestTimeToVisit: The best time to visit Uttar Pradesh is from October to March
culturalFact: Uttar Pradesh is the birthplace of Kathak, one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.

hiddenGem.name: Chitrakoot
hiddenGem.description: A scenic town in the Bundelkhand region, known for its natural beauty, ancient temples, and spiritual significance.

passportTieIn: If you have stamps or wishlist items for the Taj Mahal, Varanasi, or the Red Fort, you might want to consider visiting Uttar Pradesh next!

name: West Bengal
tagline: Where the Ganges meets the Bay of Bengal

topAttractions.name: Victoria Memorial
topAttractions.description: A stunning white marble building that serves as a museum and a tribute to Queen Victoria's legacy in India.

topAttractions.name: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway
topAttractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and a scenic train ride that passes through the picturesque Himalayan foothills.

topAttractions.name: Sundarbans National Park
topAttractions.description: The largest mangrove forest in the world, home to the Bengal tiger and a variety of other wildlife.

culturalFact: West Bengal is home to the famous Bengali renaissance movement, which saw the emergence of influential thinkers and writers like Rabindranath Tagore and Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.

hiddenGem.name: Mayapur
hiddenGem.description: A small town in Nadia district, known for its beautiful temples and the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON) headquarters.

passportTieIn: If you have stamps or wishlist items for Darjeeling, the Himalayan foothills, or the Sundarbans, you might want to consider visiting West Bengal next!
